title: CRM Org Strategy and Deployment Methodology
summary: Implementing life sciences CRM across global organizations requires a structured org strategy to balance standardization with local market flexibility. The recommended approach uses a maximum of two configuration levels: a core data model layer (global standards) and a local configuration layer (market-specific adaptations). A single Salesforce org per market is generally recommended, though multi-market orgs are possible with profile-level separation for different lines of business.

findings.implementation_phases: Kickoff workshop to define global requirements and naming conventions, followed by core data model build, local configuration adaptation, UAT, and phased market rollout. A governance board oversees configuration standards and change approval
findings.org_consolidation: Consolidating multiple existing orgs into a single org is a major undertaking requiring data migration, user re-training, and integration reconfiguration. The decision to consolidate should weigh long-term maintenance savings against short-term migration costs
findings.configuration_governance: Naming conventions must be established upfront for custom fields, objects, and metadata. Profile-based access control separates different business units within a shared org. Admin access cannot be restricted at the Salesforce license level — governance must be enforced through process, not technology
findings.deployment_tools: Metadata deployment uses change sets, IDE tooling, or CI/CD pipelines. Unmanaged packages serve as deployment units for reusable configuration bundles. Version control and sandbox-based testing are essential for multi-market rollouts

source: CRM Org Strategy and Deployment Methodology (implementation methodology, Sept 2017)
